findings.body: When `wsl --status` reports default version 1, this branch only runs `wsl --set-default-version 2`. That sets the default for future distributions; it does not enable the Virtual Machine Platform feature required for WSL2. An existing WSL1 laptop without that feature can therefore finish or retry this path without Docker's WSL2 backend working. [Microsoft's WSL installation steps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install-manual) enable the feature before setting the default version. The test at `tests/test_sales_install.py:244-256` asserts only that the insufficient command was called.
findings.title: Not done: enable WSL2 for existing WSL1 installs

findings.body: The head commit's Functional check says the prior Windows piped stub run failed its assertion and that the all-present and WSL2 guidance paths still await a Windows CI run. The plan at `plans/FORGE-SALES-1.md:81-86` requires the worker to record stubbed runs of both scripts. No successful result for those Windows paths is recorded in the supplied evidence.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

findings.body: The test accepts either the administrator path or the non-administrator message according to the runner's privilege level. The repository's Windows CI uses `windows-latest` (`.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:23-25`), and [GitHub documents that these runners run as administrators](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners). Consequently, removing the plain non-administrator next action from `scripts/install-windows.ps1:43` would leave this test green. Exercise that user-facing failure path explicitly.
findings.title: Not done: test Windows non-administrator WSL2 guidance

findings.body: Any directory with each browser prefix counts as installed, including an incomplete download or binaries from an older Playwright release; Windows makes the same check at `scripts/install-windows.ps1:21`. Check mode can report nothing missing even though the project's Playwright cannot launch a browser. [Playwright requires browser binaries matched to its version](https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers).
findings.title: Check usable Playwright browser revisions before skipping installation

findings.body: A standalone `docker` command makes this script skip Docker Desktop; Windows uses the same command-only check at `scripts/install-windows.ps1:52`. Even after a fresh Desktop installation, neither script tells the user to launch it, so setup can finish with no usable Docker engine. Check Desktop separately and give a plain first-launch action. [Docker's Mac](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/mac-install/) and [Windows](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/windows-install/) instructions both require starting Desktop after installation.
findings.title: Check Docker Desktop and tell the user to start it

findings.body: If `curl` fails, its command substitution can supply an empty string to `/bin/bash -c`; that command succeeds, so `set -e` does not stop the script at the failed download. On a Mac without Homebrew, setup then reaches `brew install` and fails with `brew: command not found` instead of explaining that the download failed and what to retry. Check the download result before invoking Bash.
findings.title: Stop when the Homebrew installer download fails
